questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: In California you get to experience a culture that is different from Europe and also a school system which works different. At the same time US is an English speaking country, which was one of the most important aspects for my study destination. I wanted to be able to speak to people right away without having to learn a totally new language. Furthermore, I also got to strengthen my English skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The school sent a lot of information due to the uncertain times, and it was easy to attend the online classes even though it was new to everyone.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because of Covid my situation was probably different than it will be in the future, as I was left kind of on my own. This was because the school were closed down the first month of school. I received a lot of emails on how to deal with online classes and I of course could always reach out to abroad office if I needed any help. But in general, all the physical welcoming programs were cancelled.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: This would have been different if Covid wasn't there.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find housing! I started living at on campus housing, but the other students living there are a lot younger than we are in Denmark when going to university. Therefore, I moved to a house off campus a month after my arrival, which I was lucky to find. I would recommend to start the housing application early in the process. There's several Facebook pages to look at if you want to live of campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is cheaper to live off campus than to live on campus, but both things are more expensive than to live in Copenhagen. I would recommend living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To study in the US you need a Visa to enter the country and because of the pandemic it was difficult to get it. also you need to take a test, to show that your English is good enough. The process can be kind of hard but it's all with it

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Copenhagen University has a person to help with any questions that come up during the application process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It is hard to get all the classes you want as an exchange student because the university prioritize their own students for the classes. But you can always crash classes you didn't get, and then you will hopefully get it anyway. I was pretty successful in getting the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were more practical than on our own university, which was nice as you got real work cases to work with. The exams are mostly multiple choice and are a lot easier than in Copenhagen I would say.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More practical and not at all as theoretical as on UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Digital Journalism, Marketing Communication, Sound Production, Media Effects on Individuals, Mindfulness, Multimedia Learning.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Marketing Communication and Digital Journalism.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In the US there's fees on everything, which should be encountered. Things are expensive in Santa Barbara. You also wanna go travel and see other places, which can be expensive too.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things were more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a huge Recreation Center for all the students to train in (there's pool too).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a club called excursion club, where you can rent surf boards, paddle boards and camping gear.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to San Francisco, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Mexico and Hawaii while I was there - and I would recommend them all. Go to Funkzone in Santa Barbara Downtown to drink wine and hear music.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy - they are different but nice everyone.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Move in to a house with American people

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They smoke a lot of weed, which is not as common for us as it is for them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they are very welcoming and love europeans.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The beach is in your backyard
2. You will never regret it
3. It will strengthen you in personal and academic ways

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I have mentioned it all

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is hard to tell, but maybe meeting all the other exchange student and creating new relationships with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning is always the toughest - but quickly it will get easier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
